newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen down on Finance One and economy.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen down on Finance One and economy.

text.p: Thai stocks are seen falling as the resumption of trade in shares of ailing Finance One Plc on Friday is set to cast a pall over the already battered market, traders said
The SET Index lost 4.66 points or 0.83 percent to 558.17 on Thursday. The SET 50 closed down 0.39 points to 40.30.

"I have seen a number of sell orders at four baht. This stock is not like BBC (Bangkok Bank of Commerce) because the foreigners own large stakes in the company and seem to want to sell at any price," said a trader at a Thai Farmers Bank affiliated broker.

Opinions vary on the extent to which a fall in Finance One's price will affect the overall market with some traders feeling the spillover will be limited by a softening of prices in the finance sector. Finance stocks lost 2.58 percent on Thursday.
"Finance stocks have been sold down already this week in preparation and to some extent Finance One's re-start may already be discounted," she said.

Other traders said they fear a spillover to other finance stocks and possibly the overall market. Losses could be pared by a commercial bank support fund which may enter the market if the banking stocks soften significantly, traders predicted.
Early bids and asks showed a wide range in early quotes on Finance One stock.
Other factors are seen having a limited impact on Thai stocks on Friday though economic concerns continue to underpin overall market sentiment, analysts said.
The market barely reacted to economic data released on Thursday which economists said showed limited signs of a turnaround.
